    I’m new to Pete Rango. What should I listen to first?

    A good starting point is "IOI (Intuition Over Intellect)", which Pete Rango says marked the start of a close friendship and unlocked something in their production styles. 2 Pete Rango also shared a rare demo, made years ago, with @oc_thumper on drums. It was a favorite among friends and was offered to mint and listen to until December 31st. 3 An interview says Pete Rango keeps a Spotify playlist of their latest collabs and releases, but the supplied text doesn't name specific tracks from it. 4

    Finding and usefulness

    Finding: A useful, supported first-listen recommendation is diluted by an unnamed old demo and a playlist reference without a usable track list.

    Usefulness: IOI (Intuition Over Intellect) is a concrete starting point with an artist-attributed reason. The recommendation is a bounded judgment, not an unsupported best-song ranking. The extra demo deadline and playlist discussion add less actionable material.

    What makes that a good introduction to his music?

    The track captures a turning point for Pete Rango: he says it marked the start of his friendship with @goalangonyc and unlocked something in their production styles. 1 It reflects the approach he describes of creating by intuition over intellect, including the lesson to "just always press record!" 1 He hopes listeners can feel how free he and @goalangonyc felt the day they chose to live by intuition. 1

    Finding and usefulness

    Finding: The follow-up preserves the actual recommended track and adds a grounded explanation of its creative significance.

    Usefulness: The intuition-over-intellect approach and just-always-press-record lesson give a listener a reason to explore IOI. The answer attributes the feeling of freedom to the artist instead of pretending to have listened to the audio.

    Follow-up continuity: Advances the actual E01 thread. Planner resolves IOI, the API topic names that track, and the displayed answer stays with its source rather than switching to the other retrieved works.

    How did Pete Rango get started making music?

    After moving to the states, their cousin André handed them 112's "Part III" and Dr. Dre's "2001", which shifted how they thought about creating music, bringing in samplers and computers beyond guitar. 2 Afterward, they started exploring drum machines and making music on their computer, though they don't recall one specific first thing they made. 1

    Usefulness: The move from guitar toward samplers, computers and drum machines is a concrete musical development. Naming the two records makes the connection worth exploring without claiming a complete biography or a first composition.
